{{short description|Russian mathematician (born 1943)}}
'''Victor Danilovich Mazurov''' ({{langx|ru|Виктор Данилович Мазуров}}; born January 31, 1943) is a Russian [[mathematician]]. He is well known for his works in [[group theory]] and is the founder of the Novosibirsk school of finite groups. Mazurov is a Corresponding Member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]].
<!-- Deleted image removed: [[File:Victor Mazurov.jpg|thumbnail|Photo of Victor Mazurov in 2010]] -->

Mazurov's parents Daniil Petrovich and Evstolia Ivanovna were teachers.<ref>Sib Math Journal, Vol. 54(1), 2013 http://math.nsc.ru/LBRT/a4/Mazurov/rus/bio_ru.htm</ref>  Victor went to elementary school in a village of Kuvashi and finished high school with highest honors in [[Zlatoust]]. He then moved to Sverdlovsk (now [[Yekaterinburg]]) to study mathematics in [[Ural State University]].  His advisers in Sverdlovsk were Victor Busarkin and Albert Starostin.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=125694}}</ref> In 1963 Mazurov married his university classmate Nadezhda Khomenko. After graduating in 1965, they moved to Novosibirsk where Mazurov joined the research staff of the Sobolev Institute of Mathematics ({{langx|ru|[[:ru:Институт математики СО РАН|Институт математики СО РАН]]}}).

Mazurov is an editor (with Evgenyj Khukhro) of the "Kourovka Notebook",<ref>{{Cite arXiv |eprint = 1401.0300|last1 = Khukhro|first1 = E. I.|title = Unsolved Problems in Group Theory. The Kourovka Notebook|last2 = Mazurov|first2 = V. D.|class = math.GR|year = 2014}}</ref> a periodically updated collection of over 1,000 open problems in Group Theory.

Mazurov obtained several results that contributed to the proof of the [[classification of finite simple groups]], also known as the Enormous Theorem<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://mathworld.wolfram.com/EnormousTheorem.html|title = Enormous Theorem}}</ref> and considered one of the greatest achievements in mathematics of the 20th century.

He is one of the initial group of [[fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{citation|title=Fellows of the AMS: Inaugural Class|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|date=May 2013|pages=631–637|url=http://www.ams.org/notices/201305/rnoti-p631.pdf|volume=60|issue=5|first=Allyn|last=Jackson}}</ref>
